The weights of watermelons produced by a certain farm are normally distributed with a mean of 4.82 kg. Long-term quality control data show that when a watermelon from this farm is randomly selected, the probability that it weighs less than 3.75 kg is $0.116$.

A watermelon is labelled as being the ideal size if it weighs between 4.82 kg and 5.89 kg.

The normal distribution is symmetric about the mean $4.82$, and $3.75$ and $5.89$ are the same distance from it:
$$4.82-3.75=1.07=5.89-4.82$$
So, by symmetry, $P(X>5.89)=P(X<3.75)=0.116$.

Half of the distribution lies above the mean, so
$$\begin{aligned} P(4.82<X<5.89)&=0.5-P(X>5.89)\\ &=0.5-0.116\\ &=0.384\end{aligned}$$

2636.stem:
The function below models the general normal distribution.

$$f(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,e^{-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2}$$

parts.latex: Show that $f'(x)$ can be written as $f'(x)=\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2}f(x)$.
Hence find $f''(x)$ in terms of $f(x)$
Show that the points of inflection for this function occur when $x$ is exactly one standard deviation from the mean $\mu$. You do not need to test or show the change in concavity at these points.

solutions.latex:
Using the chain rule on the exponent $-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2$:

$$\begin{aligned} f'(x)&=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\times2\times\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\times\dfrac{1}{\sigma}\right)e^{-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2} \\ &=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\left(-\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma^2}\right)e^{-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2} \\ &=-\dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma^2}\times\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma}\right)^2} \\ &=\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2}f(x) \end{aligned}$$

as required.
criteria: Shows some progress towards the solution, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the product rule, $\dfrac{d}{dx}(uv)=u'v+uv'$, with

$$\begin{aligned} u&=\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2} & v&=f(x) \\ u'&=-\dfrac{1}{\sigma^2} & v'&=\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2}f(x) \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} f''(x)&=u'v+uv' \\ &=-\dfrac{1}{\sigma^2}f(x)+\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2}\times\dfrac{\mu-x}{\sigma^2}f(x) \\ &=\dfrac{(\mu-x)^2}{\sigma^4}f(x)-\dfrac{f(x)}{\sigma^2} \\ &=\dfrac{f(x)}{\sigma^2}\left[\dfrac{(\mu-x)^2}{\sigma^2}-1\right] \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Uses the product rule and makes some progress towards $f''(x)$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Points of inflection occur where $f''(x)=0$:

$$\dfrac{f(x)}{\sigma^2}\left[\dfrac{(\mu-x)^2}{\sigma^2}-1\right]=0$$

Since $f(x)\ne0$, the first factor is never zero, so

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{(\mu-x)^2}{\sigma^2}-1&=0 \\ (\mu-x)^2&=\sigma^2 \\ \mu-x&=\pm\sigma \\ x&=\mu\pm\sigma \end{aligned}$$

$$\therefore\ \text{The inflections are one standard deviation either side of the mean.}$$
criteria: Sets $f''(x)=0$ and makes progress towards finding the inflection points, or equivalent merit (change in concavity not required)
